messages.author: a5e83218c834e013
messages.subject: Website Out of Sync?
parts:
I’m trying to update mc-stan.org go align with a recent
push to master on GitHub but Jenkins can’t deploy,

"Started by user Michael Betancourt

[EnvInject] - Loading node environment variables.
Building on master in workspace /Users/Shared/Jenkins/Home/jobs/Website - Push/workspace
[SSH] executing pre build script:


executing script:

cd public_html
git clean -d -x -f
git pull --ff

error: Your local changes to the following files would be overwritten by merge:
mc-stan.org/index.html
mc-stan.org/nav.js
mc-stan.org/pystan.html
mc-stan.org/source-repos.html
mc-stan.org/team.html
Please, commit your changes or stash them before you can merge.
Aborting
Updating da91b76..c2c3b3d
[SSH] exit-status: 1
Build step 'Execute shell script on remote host using ssh' marked build as failure
[SSH] executing post build script:


Finished: FAILURE"

I’ve cleaned the workspaces repeatedly to no avail. Who’s been messing
with the website locally?

messages.author: cab04b8f0759c712
messages.subject: Re: [stan-dev] Website Out of Sync?
parts:
On Thu, Mar 5, 2015 at 9:42 AM, Bob Carpenter <ca...@alias-i.com> wrote:

> On Mar 6, 2015, at 1:15 AM, Daniel Lee <bea...@alum.mit.edu> wrote:
>
> Hi Bob,
>
> Did you happen to make any changes directly on the server itself? The server is using git, so all you have to do is pull from the server.

Which server is using Git?  The one we use for web hosting?
Yes. It turns out their servers had git installed.
If so, how do I get onto that server to do a pull?
ssh. The info should be on the web interface somewhere.

I just used the GUI interface as I've always done to upload
changed pages after testing they were valid.
Ah. If there were any line ending changes or something silly like that, it would show as having local changes.

> Mike, I messed up in telling you that wiping the workspace would work. I forgot I just made the web server a git repo. This is remote. I think we can do some more git magic and nuke those changes.

What is remote?  Nuke which changes?

In the past, the Jenkins job used to pull changes from git onto the Jenkins machine, then upload to the web server. So I mistakenly thought the issue was with the copy on Jenkins.


Just FYI, if you want to push the website easily, all you have to do is run this Jenkins job:
http://d1m1s1b1.stat.columbia.edu:8080/job/Website%20-%20Push/


To log in, use your github credentials. The ssh credentials are stored in a key on the Jenkins machine, so none of the passwords are out in the open.


Daniel
